text:
chris: Quick thread — we need to choose a direction for rollout metadata schema. TL;DR: do we optimise for compactness (tiny binary/packed fields) to save on storage/ingest cost, or for expressivity (rich JSON with named fields) to make ops/debugging simpler?

alex: +1 expressive. we've been burning time decoding compact blobs during incident triage. human-readable wins for on-call. :coffee:

maria: counterpoint: telemetry and hot-paths care about size. compactness reduces DB IO and network egress. we should quantify cost delta first rather than decide on feelings.

chris: Agreed on measuring. Also consider compatibility surface: compact schemas are harder to extend safely. expressive schemas allow unknown-field forwards-compatibility. But huge objects also make traces noisy.

jess: proposal: hybrid approach — canonical minimal envelope + optional opaque extension. e.g.

```yaml
# minimal envelope (must be stable)
rollout: v1
model_id: rwd/llama-2-13b
variant: a
lease_token: "tok:abcd1234"
created_by: "alex"
created_at: 2024-06-12T15:20:00Z
# extension: arbitrary json blob for ops/debug (indexed only when flagged)
extension: {"experiments": "...", "notes": "..."}
```

This lets the runtime rely on the fixed fields while ops can opt-in to store/see the extension blob.

sam: I like that. Add a small compression header for the extension blob so we can toggle compressed vs inline. Also: we should make `lease_token` opaque but include a `lease_epoch` integer to support cheap comparisons without parsing.

alex: compatibility question — how do older clients behave if we add `lease_epoch`? we need a migration story.

maria: keep the minimal envelope strictly additive. Clients should ignore unknown fields. For the DB schema, we can add a new column `rollout_meta_v1` and deprecate the old column after a transition period.

chris: ops note: ensure the Console and traces redact `lease_token` in UI. We can show `lease_epoch` + last4 of token for debugging.

deploy-bot: Deployment preview: rollout-meta-service v0.9 -> v1.0 scheduled for 2024-06-20. See https://intra.redwood/infra/rollout-meta-rfc for the spec draft.

jess: dev tasks I'd add:
- Schema draft RFC (include minimal envelope + extension rules)
- Bench: ingest/storage delta between compact vs hybrid for our 30-day traces
- Migration plan: dual-write period + backfill script + canary read check

sam: ops tasks:
- Console changes for redact + show derived fields (lease_epoch, variant)
- Telemetry: add counters for extension blob size & presence

chris: decision for now: move forward with hybrid envelope (minimal required fields + optional extension blob). Next steps: Jess will open RFC, Maria will run cost bench, Alex will own migration plan.

alex: I'll draft the migration playbook and include a schema compatibility test harness.

maria: I'll run the bench and post results in this thread by EOD Friday.

jess: RFC opened: https://intra.redwood/rfcs/rollout-metadata-hybrid-2024 (WIP). Comments welcome.

chris: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the bench and RFC comments. :thumbsup:
